title: Seven Dimensions of Religion
objective: After this level you can use Ninian Smart's seven dimensions (ritual, story, doctrine, ethics, community, experience, material) to describe any religion beyond its beliefs.
summary: Ninian Smart described religions through seven dimensions: ritual, experience, story, doctrine, ethics, community and material forms, so a description neglects neither ideas nor practices.

cards.headline: Stop asking what religion is. Ask what a religion has.
cards.body: That was Ninian Smart's move. Hunting for one essence behind every religion, he argued, ends in vagueness. So he split religion into its sides, the way a prism splits one beam into colors.

cards.headline: Seven sides of one faith
cards.body: Smart, who became founding professor of religious studies at Lancaster University in 1967, named seven dimensions. Ritual and practice. Experience and emotion. Narrative, the sacred stories. Doctrine and philosophy. Ethics and law. The social side: the community and its institutions. And the material side. Remember Level 1's four shared things? Smart's list keeps them and adds three more.
cards.callout: Ritual, experience, story, doctrine, ethics, community, material

cards.headline: The sides work together
cards.body: The dimensions aren't separate drawers. At Passover, as Jews share the meal, they retrace the story of the Exodus from Egypt: ritual and story bound together, in Smart's words. Feeling runs through everything too. "Ritual without feeling is cold," Smart wrote, and "doctrines without awe or compassion are dry."

cards.headline: Don't forget the stuff
cards.body: The material dimension is the easiest to overlook. It covers buildings, art and the natural places held sacred, like the river Ganges, the Jordan and Mount Fuji. Smart's point was balance: a good description neglects neither ideas nor practices. Judge a religion by its beliefs alone and you've read the menu but skipped the meal.

cards.headline: A test drive on a flag
cards.body: Smart tried his list on nationalism and found many of the dimensions: anthems, flags and memorials. Yet he held that secular worldviews shouldn't really be called religions. The seven dimensions describe; they don't decide what gets the label.

cards.headline: Seven Dimensions of Religion: the takeaways
learned: Ninian Smart described religions through seven dimensions
The dimensions work together, like ritual and story at Passover
The material side counts: buildings, art and sacred places

questions.prompt: Which of these is one of Ninian Smart's seven dimensions of religion?
questions.explanation: Smart's seven: ritual, experience, narrative, doctrine, ethics, social, and material.

questions.prompt: Why did Smart describe religions through seven dimensions instead of beliefs alone?

options.label: To rank religions from simplest to richest
To give a balanced description of both ideas and practices
Because every religion has exactly seven rituals
To prove all religions teach the same thing
options.rationale: Balance, not sameness, was the point.

questions.explanation: Smart said the point of the list is a balanced description that neglects neither ideas nor practices.

questions.prompt: At Passover, Jews share a meal that retraces the Exodus story. Which two dimensions does that join?

options.label: Doctrine and material
options.rationale: The meal and story are ritual and narrative.

options.label: Ethics and social institutions
options.rationale: Close, but the pairing Smart named is ritual and story.

options.label: Experience and doctrine
options.rationale: Smart used Passover for ritual and story.

questions.explanation: Sharing the meal is ritual; the Exodus is the narrative. Smart said they are bound together.
